text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- The shop stewards of Central Organization of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK) have doubts about European economic and monetary union (EMU) and feel ignorant, an SAK poll shows.
- Finnish magazine publishing company A-lehdet and Swiss bank UBS are negotiating to link printing houses.
- U.N secretary general Kofi Annan and his wife will pay a two-day official visit to Finland in mid August.
- Ordinary bacteria which causes lung problems may also cause many heart diseases, Finnish medical study shows.
- There are no signs of economic growth slowing and annual GDP growth could reach even six percent, analysts say.
- If capital gains taxation is tightened as Finance Ministry plans it would damage entrepreneurs, says Jussi Jarventaus, chairman of the Finnish Entrepreneurs.
- Finland did not reach group of most risk-free countries in Wall Street Journal investment rating but was placed in the second tier with Hong Kong, Italy and Norway.
- Regulation of apartment rent prices should be resumed, Tenants' Federation says after strong hike in rents.
- Disputes over separation between cooperative banking centre (OPK) and regional banks group can be solved by the end of this week, group representatives say.
- Finnish forest industry invested more than ever last year in environment, about one billion markka, statistics show.
- Price of farmland has returned in the 1990s to match its productivity value, an agricultural study shows.

- Finnish parliament must restore power; it is the government which should enjoy the confidence of the parliament and not vice versa, says Martti Korhonen, chairman of the Left Alliance's parliamentary group.
